result.title: Internal Discrepancy for Contrastive Learning: Generalization Bounds and Downstream Behaviors
result.summary: Contrastive learning has emerged as a popular paradigm for training representation models. While prior studies pursue more practical and less restrictive assumptions to enhance theoretical understanding of contrastive learning, they essentially describe the interconnections among representations within the data or induced by the function class. To encapsulate these assumptions, we propose the measure of internal discrepancy that quantifies the difference between the mean representation of positive samples and latent cluster centers. We then prove an internal discrepancy-aware generalization bound for downstream supervised tasks following contrastive learning, without requiring additional assumptions. This generalization bound not only serves as a unifying framework connecting various assumptions but also motivates us to further reduce the internal discrepancy, thereby introducing the relaxed k-means loss as an approximation. Moreover, we investigate the downstream behaviors of contrastive learning from the perspective of contrastive learning-incurred supervised losses. In the presence of class imbalance, we shed light on why contrastive learning can facilitate imbalanced learning. Finally, we investigate the optimality of these incurred supervised losses, proving several intriguing properties.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「internal discrepancy」来度量正样本平均表示与潜在簇中心之间的差异，据此在无额外假设下证明对比学习后下游监督任务的泛化界，并用 relaxed k-means 损失近似降低该差异，还分析了下游监督损失的行为及类别不平衡下的作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其潜在簇中心与表示几何的泛化界分析，可能为刻画 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的结构化程度与下游收益关系提供度量视角，但迁移到视觉推理状态是否成立仍需核查。
